- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

## `Test Core (1/6)` is red, it is ⛔ NOT this PR's, and it is a NEW signature — 2026-09-22T05:37Z

Seat note from `domain:spec` seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`). Read from the job log first-hand.

**Full signature**, job `106625053057`:

> `::error file=scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs, title=[repo] src/api/error-catalog-docs.test.ts, line=1802` — `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_mz2es9op0s7.mjs'`
> `❯ walk :1802 ❯ scanSources :1817 ❯ deriveWireFace :1862 ❯ src/api/error-catalog-docs.test.ts:55`
> `Test Files 1 failed | 33 passed` · ⭐ **`Tests 580 passed (580)`**

**Initial judgment.** ⛔ Not this PR's, and ⛔ not a timeout: **no assertion failed** — the file died during collection. `walk()` stats every `readdirSync` entry unguarded, and `tsup.config.bundled_<hash>.mjs` is the temp config tsup writes and deletes around a bundle (`.gitignore:94` already declares `*.bundled_*.mjs` transient). A concurrent package build in the same workspace is the whole cause.

⭐ The sharpest part: the filter one line below `statSync` keeps only `/\.tsx?$/`, so that `.mjs` **would have been discarded anyway** — the run died on a file it did not want.

**Why not this PR's**, by file list rather than argument: this diff is `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` (one line) plus a changeset. It touches no code path this trace names.

⇒ **Filed as #19667** with the code reading and the blast radius.

⇒ This PR stays watched until green, merged or closed. ⚠️ Note for whoever lands it: this signature can hit **any** PR whose CI overlaps a tsup bundle, so a second red here is ⛔ not evidence about this diff either.

## Why this PR sat red for seven hours — and what actually failed

Measured at 2026-09-22T12:55Z on run [35690079389](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/35690079389), attempt 1, head `5ac6291a99`. Newest run per check name; no later run of that name existed.

**The failing check is `Test Core (1/6)`, and no test assertion failed in it:**

```
Test Files  1 failed | 33 passed (34)
Tests       580 passed (580)
```

The failure is in a repo-scan step, not a test body:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat
  '…/packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_mz2es9op0s7.mjs'
  at walk → scanSources → deriveWireFace
  scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs:1802
```

`tsup` writes `packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_<random>.mjs`, reads it, and deletes it. The conformance scan walks the tree concurrently and `stat`s every entry it enumerated. When the delete lands between the `readdir` and the `stat`, the scan throws on a file that is *supposed* to be gone. The random infix in the filename is itself the tell: nothing in a diff can name that path, and no two runs produce the same one.

**Not this PR's.** The diff is two files — `.changeset/19269-liveness-readme-lint-path.md` and `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`. No TypeScript, no published bytes outside one Markdown file. `main` was measured green at `fb7b7469` (`ci.yml` and `lint.yml` both `completed/success`), so this is not inherited breakage either.

**Why it stayed red.** Not CI — me. The seat recorded this PR as "watched" at 2026-09-22T05:51Z and did not come back to it. The seat's own patrol routine listed only the cards it was actively dispatching, so this PR was never re-read. The list was hand-written; that is the root cause, and the routine is being changed to query GitHub for every open PR under this identity instead of reading a list the seat wrote down. Writing a value into a note and then reading the note instead of the world is the same failure shape twice in one session.

**Why it was not simply re-run.** The fleet App identity cannot mint a token through this container's proxy — `POST /app/installations/163654544/access_tokens` answers `403 Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy`, re-measured at 2026-09-22T12:55Z. A re-run under the seat's ordinary account identity is not one of the three uses that account is permitted, so that route is ⛔ closed rather than merely inconvenient.

**What was done instead.** `origin/main` merged into this branch at `d1c22352aa`, so CI re-measures the same two-file diff against the current green `main`. The merge is clean and the PR's own contribution is byte-unchanged — `git diff` against the new merge-base is still exactly those two files. ⛔ No rebase, no force-push, no empty commit, and no test skipped, disabled or quarantined.

**Filed, not buried.** The scan/`tsup` race is a real defect in shared CI infrastructure that can redden any PR in the repo, so it gets its own card rather than a shrug — whoever finds a flake fixes it or files it.
